source.title: Deep models reveal better strategies for superposition

record.file_problem: The article is present in full, but many mathematical expressions and some numerical values are missing or stripped in the web text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports results on superposition geometry in toy networks, but does not test the listed claims about neuron-pole explanations, interpretability rates, or explanation evaluation.
record.gate_note: The study's own toy-network results on how decoder depth relates to feature-embedding geometry are recorded as findings outside the listed versions. Results cited from prior work are not recorded. Reconstruction-MSE comparisons are not included because they do not measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: A toy superposition study: 4 features in a 2D bottleneck with bilinear decoders of varying depth, measuring embedding geometry and MSE. It audits no neurons, scores no neuron explanations, builds no attribution graphs and uses no InceptionV1 or language models, so it bears on none of V1–V7. Its discussion that expressive downstream computation makes clean symmetric structures unlikely is speculation, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct, with one addition. The authors also argue that uniform polytope geometries come from shallow decoders rather than from superposition itself. They add that feature-direction norms may not reliably indicate a feature's importance. Transfer to real networks is untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a synthetic four-feature, two-dimensional encoder-decoder reconstruction task, varying bilinear decoder depth and measuring MSE and embedding geometry. It does not audit neuron poles or test explanations on activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported geometry strategy varies with decoder depth. The study also reports that binned-decoder resolution affects the preferred geometry and that longer training changes the deeper model's residual MSE gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 20 runs per depth, tied ReLU and 1-bilinear-layer models gave symmetric antipodal pairs in 19/20 runs. Deeper decoders mostly gave asymmetric pairs, and asymmetric-plus-opened pairs at 3–4 layers (14/20 and 10/20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy 4-feature, 2D superposition, decoder expressivity (depth) determines whether models use symmetric, asymmetric or opened antipodal embedding geometries.

fits_no_version.finding: The single bilinear MLP matches the best quadratic decoder (MSE gap 0.0%). The four-layer model keeps an MSE gap of about 18% that does not close with longer training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deeper bilinear decoders in toy superposition tasks fall short of the best decoder in their function class.

record.problems: The reported experiments use a small synthetic setup with four features and a two-dimensional bottleneck. The authors state that higher-dimensional bottlenecks and transfer to real networks remain future work. The web text also omits some equations and numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: MSE comparisons and theoretical decoder calculations in Sections 3 and 5 were left out because they do not measure any listed claim version; no omitted results from the strategy-classification table.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-share estimates.
No language models, MoE models or scale sweep.
No InceptionV1 or cat-and-car neuron analysis; superposition is only studied in a synthetic toy.
Decoder depth changes embedding geometry, but no neuron interpretability shares, tools, regularization or vision-model estimates are measured.
No attribution graphs or circuit units.
No neuron explanations from activating examples.
No automated simulation scoring of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The rows faithfully reproduce the Section 4 table. No row bears on any version, so the 'none' links and the T6/discusses classification stand.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or estimates of one-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No language models, dense or mixture-of-experts models, or model-scale sweep.
No InceptionV1 neurons, cat-and-car example, or test of pose as a shared feature.

The study varies toy decoder depth and reports changes in feature-embedding geometry, but does not measure neuron interpretability shares, late-layer neurons, regularization, tools, or vision-model estimates.
No attribution graphs or test of whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
No neuron explanations evaluated on activating examples or tested for prediction of firing.
No automated neuron-explanation scoring on new text.
